name: Required Game Settings
summary: The exact in-game values XIM needs for your game. Set them, and leave everything else at default.

where.text: Not a setting: these are values you set in your game. To review the required in-game settings for your game, press the gear icon on Manager's main screen, the Dashboard.

citations.quote: If you need to check required in-game settings at a later time, press the gear icon on Manager's main screen.
Use the gear icon to review the required in-game settings for the game.

definition.text: When you add a Config, you may be reminded to set the game's sensitivity to maximum. There may also be game-specific settings you must follow. The rest should stay at default.

citations.quote: When a new Xbox Config is added to your XIM MATRIX, you may be reminded that you must set your game's in-game sensitivity to maximum (aim sensitivity is then customized in your Config).
In all cases, there may be additional game-specific setting requirements you will need to follow. The rest of the settings should be remain at default.

plainWords.text: XIM keeps a list per game. Its public copy says every game needs maximum in-game sensitivity and default values, unless the list says otherwise. Some games need extra settings.

citations.quote: XIM’s Smart Translation technology requires that your game be set up to its maximum in-game sensitivity and all other values as default unless otherwise stated for accurate aim response.
The following games require additional in-game settings (failure to do so will result sub-optimal aiming performance):

plainWords.caveat: This comes from a public copy of XIM's forum list of game settings. It may differ from the current login-walled list, so confirm in Manager (gear icon on the main screen).

plainWords.text: Maximum sensitivity is what Standard sync asks for, and every game has Standard. XIM's guide also describes cases where your in-game sensitivity is not at maximum. With Custom sync (only in games that support it), you choose your own in-game aim settings, such as Hip and ADS sensitivity, and copy them into your Config. Manual sync calibrates to your own in-game settings, but XIM discourages it for controller output. If you turn on Simulate Analog Behavior (SAB), XIM says to lower in-game sensitivity so it is not at or near maximum, and all other settings must still match the required list.

citations.quote: Every game that XIM MATRIX supports has the standard game settings synchronization option.
Sensitivity is set to maximum
Custom is a powerful synchronization option that let's you choose your game's aim settings including:
Hip and ADS sensitivity
To use, copy your game's aim settings into your Config:
The manual synchronization method is an advanced option that lets you calibrate to your particular set of in-game aim settings.
Manual reticle velocity calibration for Configs that output as controller may not produce accurate results and is thus discouraged from being used.
Or, if you are a controller gamer (and the game has support for it), aim is customized in your game and settings are copied to your Config.
When using SAB, you will need to turn your game's aim sensitivity down so it's not at or near maximum.
Other than lowering your in-game sensitivity, ensure all other game settings match those listed on the official required game settings list.

plainWords.text: The game's deadzone settings must match the required ones.

citations.quote: Your game's deadzone settings must match the required settings for your game.

plainWords.text: Some games have extra input requirements, such as needing Simulate Analog Behavior (SAB). The list says so in those games' entries.

citations.quote: Input Requirements: This game has additional input requirements that must be observed in order to play. With a XIM MATRIX, it is required that Simulate Analog Behavior (SAB) be enabled.
citations.note: How the page marks games that need SAB, here in the Apex Legends (ALC) entry.

guidance.text: Get them wrong and your aim suffers. Configs shared by others won't work properly either.

citations.quote: Failure to configure your game's required settings correctly will result in negative aiming performance and the inability to effectively share and use Configs from others.

guidance.text: Check them any time with the gear icon on Manager's main screen.

citations.quote: If you need to check required in-game settings at a later time, press the gear icon on Manager's main screen.

guidance.caveat: The public copy of XIM's forum list of game settings may differ from the current list. Treat Manager's list as the one to match.

guidance.text: When checking cm/360, XIM says the required settings must be correct and all others must be default, such as FOV.

citations.quote: Your in-game required settings are correct and all others are default (such as FOV)

confusions.name: Custom in-game settings
confusions.note: With Custom sync you choose some in-game values yourself. The other required settings still apply.
